requirements.requirement: /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance exists as a valid, executable script producing correct output
requirements.summary: Initial inspection (cmd-90b9bf6092934deb) revealed the file at /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance contained leftover heredoc/chmod text rather than a valid script and was not executable (mode 644 per prepare baseline). Executor rewrote it with a valid #!/bin/sh script and set mode 0755 root:root (cmd-07be980023f346f7), then confirmed correct output via manual invocation (cmd-0fe16a0e76d84319) and again post-restart (cmd-a3ee91220c10430c).

requirements.requirement: Cron entry scheduled to run the script daily at 02:15
requirements.summary: Root's crontab was updated to include '15 2 * * * /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance >> /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log 2>&1' (cmd-1559fd7600f94c22), correctly encoding 02:15 daily, and the entry was confirmed present both before and after the node restart (cmd-ee35651cc3e9437c, cmd-a3ee91220c10430c).

requirements.requirement: Cron daemon is active/enabled so the schedule will actually execute
requirements.summary: crond was found stopped (cmd-90b9bf6092934deb); executor added it to the default runlevel and started it, confirmed 'status: started' and present in 'rc-update show default' (cmd-261096fda74047be). Post-restart, crond was confirmed auto-started and running (cmd-a3ee91220c10430c), demonstrating persistence of the enablement across reboot.

Manual invocation of the exact crontab command line appended a timestamped completion line to /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log (cmd-0fe16a0e76d84319). Post-restart, the log file was shown to have persisted the earlier entry plus a new appended entry from a fresh run (cmd-a3ee91220c10430c), confirming durable, correct log capture.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1 with full pre/post transition evidence
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id c3c51c23... with crond started and cron entry present (cmd-ee35651cc3e9437c, cross-checked by global:after_prepare:node1:boot-identity). A background-delayed reboot was issued and acknowledged (cmd-4e01f5f31a7b40d9) before the connection dropped (cmd-e68914cdb77b4220 through cmd-c3674309e0204df6 show expected disconnection/reconnection polling). A new boot_id 7e6cd366... was observed after reconnection (cmd-45bfdef571324870), matching the fixed global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity snapshot, and post-restart state showed crond running, cron entry intact, script executable, and log data persisted plus a new successful run (cmd-a3ee91220c10430c).

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task contract are satisfied: the script was found broken and repaired to a valid executable, a correctly-formed 02:15 daily cron entry was added, crond was enabled and started, and the log file was shown to capture script output correctly, including after a validated reboot cycle. The independent node-restart protocol was also fully and coherently demonstrated with a clean baseline, acknowledged restart, changed boot identity, and full post-restart recovery of cron/service/script/log state, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Only a minor, low-risk residue (/tmp/reboot.log) was left over from the restart mechanism.
limitations: The prepared baseline recorded the script as having hash 385431df... with 644 permissions and no executable bit; the executor's inspection (cmd-90b9bf6092934deb) found different, malformed content, consistent with a heredoc/chmod leftover — this is treated as a pre-existing defect the executor was required to fix rather than executor-caused damage, but the exact original byte-for-byte state relies on a single cat command.

No direct evidence of an actual scheduled 02:15 cron firing was captured (expected, since the evaluation window did not span an actual 02:15 occurrence); correctness of scheduled execution is inferred from crontab syntax and successful manual invocation of the identical command line.
Failed-services checks were unsupported on this Alpine/OpenRC platform (no systemctl), limiting cross-validation of service health beyond the explicit crond status checks performed.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor commands were reviewed in order: discovery/inspection (cmd-b7c2fc789edc414c, cmd-90b9bf6092934deb) were read-only and revealed the script was broken; the rewrite (cmd-07be980023f346f7) was a necessary corrective mutation directly required by the task contract. The crontab edit (cmd-1559fd7600f94c22) and crond enable/start (cmd-261096fda74047be) are both required for the schedule to function. The manual script run to seed/verify the log (cmd-0fe16a0e76d84319) and the later verification run (cmd-a3ee91220c10430c) are bounded evidence-collection actions. The reboot (cmd-4e01f5f31a7b40d9) was required by the independent node-restart protocol, was low-risk and single-node, and was fully validated with recovery evidence. The many connection-reset/timeout polling commands during the reboot window (cmd-e68914cdb77b4220 through cmd-c3674309e0204df6) are read-only polling attempts, not mutations. One minor residue was left behind: /tmp/reboot.log, created as a side effect of the backgrounded 'nohup sh -c sleep 2; reboot' command (cmd-4e01f5f31a7b40d9), and it was not cleaned up (visible in global:after_executor:node1:temporary-files). This is a small, low-risk, non-sensitive artifact but represents unretracted residue.
